unit.title: Clean and maintain soft floor and furnishings

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Which of these are "soft floors and furnishings" in a hotel or villa?
options: Tiled floors, marble steps and wooden decks
Glass tables, mirrors, lamps and metal patio chairs
Pots, pans and other kitchen equipment
Carpets, rugs, curtains, cushions and upholstery

questions.stem: Why should you check the fibre or care label of a carpet or sofa before cleaning it?
options: To find out how old the carpet or sofa is
Some fibres shrink, fade or run if cleaned the wrong way
To find out which shop it was bought from
The label tells you which room it should go in

questions.stem: Why is regular vacuuming the most important job in caring for carpets?
options: It is the only way to remove deep stains like red wine or coffee
It means the carpet never needs a deep clean again
It removes grit that cuts the fibres and wears the carpet
It makes the carpet smell of the cleaning products

questions.stem: Where in a hotel does carpet usually get dirty and worn fastest?
options: At doorways, in corridors and in front of chairs
Under the beds and behind large, heavy wardrobes
In the corners of rooms no one uses
Under the curtains by the windows

questions.stem: Before you vacuum a guest room, what should you check on the vacuum cleaner?
options: The plug and cable are undamaged and the bag is not full
That it has been left plugged in and running since the last room
That the bag is full, so it picks up more dust
That the guest knows how to use it if they need it

questions.stem: Why must you never use an ordinary dry vacuum cleaner to pick up water?
options: The water will make the dust bag smell of soap for weeks
The water will stop the brushes from turning
Water can cause an electric shock and ruin the motor
Water makes the vacuum too heavy to push about

questions.stem: When vacuuming a corridor, how should you manage the cable?
options: Run it across the corridor so guests can see it
Keep it behind you and to one side, out of walkways
Pull the vacuum along by the cable to move it
Plug it in at the far end so that it stretches tight all the way

questions.stem: You are using a carpet cleaning chemical in a small room. What should you do?
options: Close the windows and door to keep the smell in
Spray it into the air to freshen up the room
Mix it with bleach to make it work faster
Wear gloves and keep the room well aired

questions.stem: What is the best way to vacuum a carpet?
options: Fast, single strokes in one direction only
Only down the middle of the room, where most people walk
Slow, overlapping strokes, with the edges done as well
Pushing hard on the handle to dig the dust out

questions.stem: Which vacuum tool is best for cleaning along skirting boards and in corners?
options: The crevice tool (the long, narrow nozzle)
The wide floor head with the brush roll turning
The round dusting brush for lampshades
No tool; corners do not need cleaning

questions.stem: How should you vacuum upholstered chairs and sofa cushions?
options: Use the main floor head, with the brush roll turning fast
Use the upholstery tool and do both sides of the cushions
Beat them with a broom handle outside instead
Vacuum only the parts the guest can see

questions.stem: Why should you pick up hairpins, coins and earrings before vacuuming?
options: They make the carpet look untidy in photographs
Guests may want to count them on their return
The vacuum works better with something to pick up
They can damage the vacuum and may be guest property

questions.stem: The vacuum cleaner starts to smell of burning. What should you do?
options: Switch it off, unplug it and report it
Carry on, as the smell will soon go away by itself
Pour some water into it to cool the motor down
Open a window and finish the room first

questions.stem: Why should you check and clean the vacuum's filter as the maker says?
options: A dirty filter makes the machine quieter for guests
The filter is where the guest's lost items are kept
A blocked filter lowers suction and can overheat the motor
A clean filter means that the bag never needs to be emptied

questions.stem: A guest spills coffee on the bedroom carpet. What should you do first?
options: Leave it to dry first so that it is easier to brush out later
Rub it hard with a wet cloth to work it loose
Pour bleach on it so the brown colour goes
Blot up as much as you can with a clean, dry cloth

questions.stem: Why do you blot a stain instead of rubbing it?
options: Rubbing uses too much of the stain remover
Rubbing spreads the stain and hurts the fibres
Blotting is faster, so the guest does not see it
Rubbing makes the cloth wear out too quickly

questions.stem: When you apply a stain remover, in which direction should you work?
options: From the outside edge of the stain towards the middle
From the middle of the stain out to the clean carpet
In large circles over the whole carpet
Up and down across the stain with a hard brush

questions.stem: Why should you test a stain remover on a hidden part of the carpet or fabric first?
options: To find out how many stains the carpet has on it
To make sure there is enough of it in the bottle
To check it does not bleach or damage the fabric
To let the fabric get used to the product slowly

questions.stem: A child has dropped chewing gum on a hotel lounge carpet. What usually works best?
options: Pull it out quickly with your fingers while it is soft
Harden it with ice or a freeze spray, then lift it off
Pour hot water on it to melt it into the carpet
Cut the carpet round it with scissors

questions.stem: Wearing gloves, which water should you use first on a fresh blood stain on fabric?
options: Boiling water, to kill the germs at once
Hot water from the tap, with bleach added
Warm water with a little cooking oil in it
Cold water, as hot water can set the stain

questions.stem: A guest has dropped sunscreen, an oily stain, on a sofa. What type of product is usually needed?
options: Plain cold water only, because oil mixes with water
A spray of bleach to lift the colour out of it
A grease spotter that suits the fabric's label
Furniture polish, rubbed well into the cushion

questions.stem: What should you do if you cannot remove a stain?
options: Report it so a specialist or deep clean can be arranged
Cover it with a rug or move a chair so that no one will see it
Keep putting on more and more remover until it goes
Cut the stained part out of the carpet with scissors

questions.stem: What does a hot water extraction machine (often called a "steam cleaner") do?
options: It blows steam over the carpet, then leaves it to dry alone
It sprays solution into the pile and sucks it back out
It brushes dry powder into the carpet using a pad
It heats the carpet to kill insects without water

questions.stem: Why must you not over-wet a carpet when deep cleaning it?
options: The carpet will dry too fast in the sun and fade
The machine will run out of solution too quickly
Wet carpet is easier for guests to walk on
It can shrink, smell, grow mould or stain from below

questions.stem: Before deep cleaning a carpet with a machine, what should you do first?
options: Spray the whole carpet with stain remover and leave it
Wet the carpet with a bucket of hot water
Move the furniture and vacuum the carpet well
Put plastic over the carpet to keep the heat in

questions.stem: Some carpets are cleaned with a dry powder (dry compound). Why might a hotel choose this method?
options: The room can be used again soon, as little water is used
It is the only method that removes oily stains
It makes the carpet much wetter and cleaner
It does not need any vacuuming before or after

questions.stem: What is the best way to help a carpet dry after deep cleaning?
options: Close the room up tight to keep all the heat in
Air the room and use fans or air conditioning
Walk on it often to press the water out of it
Lay old towels and newspapers over the wet carpet

questions.stem: Why should you not put furniture back on a damp carpet straight away?
options: The furniture will slide about on the wet pile
Damp carpet makes the furniture too heavy to move
Guests prefer to see the room without furniture
Wood stain or metal rust can mark the wet carpet

questions.stem: Why does damp carpet in a closed villa room soon start to smell musty in Jamaica's climate?
options: Mould and mildew grow fast in warm, damp places
The cleaning solution turns sour in sunlight
Sea water comes up through the floor tiles at night
Lizards and frogs are drawn to wet carpets

questions.stem: Many sofas have a cleaning code on the label. What does the code "X" usually mean?
options: Wash it in hot water with plenty of detergent
Clean it with a strong solvent, rubbed in hard
Vacuum or brush only; use no liquid cleaner
Send it to the laundry with the bed sheets

questions.stem: Why should you turn and plump the seat cushions on a sofa when you clean?
options: To hide stains under the cushion from the guest
So that the zip is always on show at the front
Guests like the cushions placed upside down
So they wear evenly and keep their shape

questions.stem: A sofa cushion cover has a zip. Should you take it off and wash it?
options: Yes, always; a zip means the cover is made to be washed
Only if the care label says so, as covers can shrink
Yes, in very hot water to kill any germs in it
No, zipped covers can only be cleaned by guests

questions.stem: How are curtains usually kept free of dust between deep cleans?
options: By shaking them out of the window each morning
By spraying them with water and leaving them to dry
By vacuuming them gently with a soft brush tool
By keeping them closed all day and night

questions.stem: Before taking down curtains to be cleaned, what should you check?
options: The care label, and that the hooks and rail are sound
That the guest has agreed to pay for the cleaning
That the windows are wide open so that the breeze can help
That someone is ready to hold the chair you stand on

questions.stem: Why do curtains and soft furnishings in sunny Jamaican rooms often fade?
options: The cold air from the air conditioning bleaches the colours out
Strong sunlight breaks down the dyes in the fabric
They are washed with too little detergent
Sea breezes blow the colour out of the cloth

questions.stem: How should you vacuum a rug with a fringe (loose threads at the ends)?
options: Run the brush roll over the fringe to straighten it
Pull the fringe straight by hand, then vacuum it hard
Cut off the fringe so it does not get caught
Keep the brush roll off the fringe; brush it straight

questions.stem: Why should rugs be turned round from time to time?
options: So guests think a new rug has been bought for them
So the stains on the back can dry out in the air
So they wear and fade more evenly
So that the pattern faces the window

questions.stem: What is the best way to stop sand and dirt from being walked into villa carpets?
options: Use mats at the doors and clean them often
Ask guests to walk on the tiles only
Spray the carpets with water every morning
Keep the doors and windows closed all day

questions.stem: After shampooing, why might a carpet be brushed with a carpet rake or brush?
options: To pull out loose threads so the carpet looks new
To push the cleaning solution deeper into the backing
To make patterns that show where it was missed
To lift the pile so it dries well and looks even

questions.stem: Small holes appear in a wool rug and you see tiny grubs (larvae). What are they most likely to be?
options: Termites that have come up from the wooden floor
Moths or carpet beetles, which eat wool
Ants looking for crumbs left by guests
Mosquito larvae from the swimming pool

questions.stem: While cleaning you find a cigarette burn in a carpet. What should you do?
options: Report it, as it may need a repair or a charge
Rub ash into it so it matches the colour
Move a chair over it before the guest returns
Cut out the burnt fibres and say nothing

questions.stem: How can you check that a carpet has been vacuumed fully?
options: Ask the guest to look under the bed for you
Feel it with your bare feet when nobody is about
Look for even stroke lines and no grit in the corners
Smell the carpet to see if it smells of the cleaner

questions.stem: What should you do with a carpet extraction machine after use?
options: Leave the dirty water in it for the next job
Empty and rinse both tanks, and clean the nozzle
Store it with the solution tank full and closed
Wipe the outside only, as the inside cleans itself

questions.stem: A wet rug is too heavy to carry outside to dry. What should you do?
options: Drag it across the floor by one of its corners
Fold it over your shoulder and run with it
Leave it in a heap in the corner to drain
Get help, or roll it and use a trolley

questions.stem: When is the best time to deep clean the carpet in a guest room?
options: While the guest is having a nap in the afternoon
On the morning that a new guest is due to arrive at the villa
When the room is empty and not booked for some hours
In the evening, while guests are getting ready

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

What colour should the cloth be that you use to blot a stain, so that no dye comes off it?
What type of vacuum cleaner is worn on the cleaner's back?
On a sofa's cleaning code, what does the letter "W" stand for?

What type of vacuum cleaner can safely pick up water as well as dust?

What is the name of the rod or track that curtains hang from?

essays.stem: Describe how to vacuum a guest room carpet thoroughly and safely.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the vacuum cleaner first: the plug and cable must have no cuts or burns, and the bag or bin must not be full. I pick up any small items such as coins, hairpins, earrings and paper clips, because they damage the machine and may belong to the guest. I move light furniture such as chairs and the luggage rack. I plug in near the door and keep the cable behind me. I start at the far corner and work back towards the door, so I do not walk on the clean carpet. I push the vacuum slowly forwards and back in overlapping strokes, which picks up more grit than fast strokes. I use the crevice tool along the skirting boards, in corners and under the bed edges, and the upholstery tool on chairs. I put the furniture back. Last, I look across the carpet for even lines and missed grit, then switch off, unplug, wind the cable loosely and empty the bag if needed.
markingPoints: Checks plug, cable and bag before use
Picks up small items and moves light furniture
Keeps the cable behind and works from the far corner to the door
Slow, overlapping strokes and tools for edges and upholstery
Checks the result, puts furniture back and switches off and unplugs

essays.stem: Explain the general steps for removing a fresh stain from a carpet or sofa.
essays.modelAnswer: The sooner a stain is treated, the easier it is to remove, so I act at once. First I scrape off any solid matter with a blunt knife or spoon, working towards the middle. Then I blot up as much liquid as I can with a clean, white, dry cloth, pressing and lifting, not rubbing, because rubbing spreads the stain and damages the fibres. I try to find out what the stain is, because different stains need different products. I read the label of the stain remover and test it on a small hidden area first, to make sure it does not bleach or damage the fabric. I wear gloves. I put a little of the product onto the cloth, not too much onto the carpet, and work from the outside of the stain towards the middle so it does not spread. I blot again, then rinse with a little clean water and blot dry. I lift the pile with my fingers or a brush. If the stain stays, I report it.
markingPoints: Acts quickly and scrapes off solids
Blots with a clean white cloth, never rubs
Finds out the stain type and tests the product on a hidden area
Applies a little product and works from the outside in, with gloves
Rinses, blots dry, grooms the pile, and reports stains that remain

essays.stem: Describe how you would deal with three stains a villa might have: spilled rum punch on a carpet, chewing gum on a rug, and sunscreen on a sofa.
essays.modelAnswer: Rum punch has sugar and red colouring, so I deal with it at once. I blot up as much as I can with a clean white cloth, then apply a little cool water or a stain remover that suits the carpet, tested on a hidden spot first. I work from the outside in and blot again, then rinse and blot dry, because sugar left in the pile goes sticky and attracts ants. For chewing gum, I harden it with a bag of ice or a freeze spray made for carpets. When it is hard and brittle, I lift or chip it off with a blunt knife, then treat any mark left with a spotter. For sunscreen, which is oily, I first scrape off what is on top, then check the sofa's cleaning code. If it allows, I use a grease spotter made for that fabric, put on a cloth, and blot. I never soak the cushion. If a stain will not come out, I report it.
markingPoints: Rum punch: blot quickly, cool water or suitable remover, rinse out the sugar
Gum: harden with ice or freeze spray, then lift off
Sunscreen: scrape, check the cleaning code, use a grease spotter on a cloth
Tests products first and works from the outside in
Does not over-wet; reports stains that remain

essays.stem: Describe how to deep clean a carpet with a hot water extraction machine.
essays.modelAnswer: I plan the job for a time when the room is empty and not needed for some hours, so it can dry. I check the machine, plug and cable. I move the furniture out, or put foil or plastic blocks under legs that cannot be moved. I vacuum the carpet well first, because dry dirt is easier to remove dry. I treat heavy stains and the worst traffic areas with a pre-spray, as the label says. I mix the cleaning solution exactly as the label says and fill the clean tank. I wear gloves. I start at the far side of the room and work back to the door. I spray and suck back in slow, overlapping strokes, and I make extra dry passes without spraying to pull out as much water as I can, so the carpet is not over-wetted. I groom the pile with a carpet brush. I air the room and use fans or the air conditioning to dry it. Last, I empty and rinse both tanks and clean the machine.
markingPoints: Plans for an empty room, checks the machine and moves or protects furniture
Vacuums well first and pre-treats stains and traffic areas
Mixes solution as the label says and wears gloves
Works from the far side with overlapping strokes and dry passes, not over-wetting
Grooms, dries with airflow, then empties, rinses and cleans the machine

essays.stem: Explain why fast drying matters in Jamaica's climate, and how you dry carpets and soft furnishings after cleaning.
essays.modelAnswer: Jamaica is warm and often humid, especially in the rainy season. If a carpet, rug, cushion or curtain stays damp for a long time, mould and mildew grow quickly. This causes a musty smell, black spots and stains, and can make guests with asthma or allergies ill. Damp carpet can also shrink, and the backing can rot. Wood stain or rust from furniture legs can mark it. To dry soft furnishings quickly I do not over-wet them in the first place, and I make extra dry passes with the extraction machine. I open windows if the air outside is dry, or I run the air conditioning or a dehumidifier and use fans pointed across the carpet. I groom the pile so air gets in. I keep people and furniture off until it is dry, and put foil or blocks under legs. Rugs and cushion covers can be dried flat in the shade outside, out of strong sun that fades colour. I check it is fully dry before the room is used.
markingPoints: Warm, humid weather lets mould and mildew grow on damp fabric
Names the effects: smell, stains, health, shrinking or rotting
Avoids over-wetting and makes extra dry passes
Uses airflow: fans, air conditioning, dehumidifier, open windows when dry outside
Keeps furniture and people off, dries outside in shade, and checks it is fully dry

essays.stem: Describe how to clean and care for an upholstered sofa in a villa, including how you use its cleaning code.
essays.modelAnswer: I vacuum the sofa regularly with the upholstery tool, including under and between the cushions and down the sides, where sand, crumbs and coins collect. I use the crevice tool in the seams. I turn and plump the cushions so they wear evenly and keep their shape. Before I use any liquid, I read the care label and its cleaning code. Many sofas use W for water-based cleaners, S for solvent cleaners only, W/S for either, and X for vacuum or brush only, with no liquid at all. I follow the code and the maker's instructions, and I test any product on a hidden spot first. For spills I blot quickly with a clean white cloth and use the right spotter on a cloth, not poured on. I do not soak the cushions. I only take off zipped covers to wash if the label allows, because they can shrink. I keep the sofa out of strong sun, and I report tears, burns, loose buttons and stains I cannot remove.
markingPoints: Vacuums regularly with upholstery and crevice tools, including under cushions
Turns and plumps cushions
Reads the cleaning code and explains W, S, W/S and X
Tests first, blots spills and uses the right spotter without soaking
Protects from sun and reports damage

essays.stem: Describe how to care for the curtains and sheers in a hotel room, including how they are taken down for cleaning.
essays.modelAnswer: Curtains and sheers collect dust, salt and insects, especially near open windows by the sea. Each week, or as the schedule says, I vacuum them gently from top to bottom with the soft brush tool, and I check the hems, hooks and rail. I check that they open and close smoothly and hang evenly. When they need a deep clean, I read the care label to see if they are washed, dry cleaned or cleaned on site. I take them down using a checked stepladder, never a chair, with a partner to take the weight, because wet or heavy curtains are awkward. I remove the hooks, count them and keep them in a bag. I fold the curtains carefully and label them with the room number so they come back to the right room. Sheers are delicate, so they are washed gently as the label says. When they are clean, they are hung back with all the hooks, checked for an even hang, and any damage is reported.
markingPoints: Regular vacuuming from top to bottom with a soft brush
Checks hems, hooks, rail and smooth running
Reads the care label to choose the cleaning method
Takes down safely with a checked stepladder and a partner, keeping and counting hooks
Labels for the room, rehangs evenly and reports damage

essays.stem: Explain the main safety points when cleaning soft floors and furnishings.
essays.modelAnswer: Electrical safety comes first. I check the plug and cable of every vacuum and machine before use, and I do not use anything with damage; I tag it and report it. I never use a dry vacuum on water, and I keep cables and plugs away from wet carpet. I switch off and unplug before changing tools, emptying the bag or clearing a blockage. I keep cables behind me and out of walkways so no one trips. Chemicals such as carpet shampoo and spotters must be used as the label and SDS say. I measure them, never mix products, wear gloves and eye protection where needed, and keep the room aired. I store them closed and labelled. Wet carpet and wet tile edges are slippery, so I put out wet floor signs and wear non-slip shoes. Wet rugs and curtains are heavy, so I get help, roll rugs and use a trolley. I use a checked stepladder for curtains and never stand on furniture.
markingPoints: Checks electrical equipment and tags faulty items
No dry vacuum on water; unplugs before changing tools or emptying
Keeps cables out of walkways
Uses chemicals as the label and SDS say, with PPE and airflow, never mixing
Wet floor signs, safe lifting with help, and a checked stepladder

essays.stem: Explain how a villa can make its carpets and rugs last longer and look good.
essays.modelAnswer: Most damage to carpets comes from grit walked in on shoes, so the villa uses barrier mats inside and outside each door and cleans them often, especially near the beach where sand is carried in. Carpets are vacuumed every day in busy areas and on a schedule elsewhere, with slow, overlapping strokes. Spills are treated at once, because fresh stains come out much more easily than old ones. Rugs are turned round from time to time so they wear and fade evenly, and furniture is moved a little so the pile does not stay crushed. Blinds or curtains are closed in the strongest sun, because sunlight fades colours. Carpets are deep cleaned on a schedule, when rooms are empty, and dried quickly so mould does not grow. Staff check for signs of moths or carpet beetles, loose edges, burns and tears, and report them so they are fixed early. Keeping a record of cleans and repairs helps plan the work.
markingPoints: Barrier mats at doors, cleaned often
Regular vacuuming, and spills treated at once
Rugs turned and furniture moved to spread wear
Protection from strong sun
Scheduled deep cleans, quick drying, and checks for pests and damage, with records

essays.stem: Compare three ways of cleaning a carpet beyond vacuuming: bonnet cleaning, dry compound and hot water extraction. Say when you might choose each one.
essays.modelAnswer: Bonnet cleaning uses a rotary machine with a round absorbent pad, called a bonnet, which is dampened with cleaning solution. The spinning pad lifts dirt from the top of the pile. Very little water is used, so the carpet dries fast. It is good for busy areas such as corridors between deep cleans, but it does not clean deep down. Dry compound is a damp powder with cleaning agents in it. It is spread on the carpet, brushed in by machine to soak up the dirt, left for a short time, and then vacuumed out. It uses almost no water, so the room can be used again soon, and it suits carpets that should not get wet. Hot water extraction sprays cleaning solution into the pile and sucks it straight back out with the dirt. It gives the deepest clean, but the carpet stays damp for some hours. It is best done on a schedule when the room is empty and can be aired.
markingPoints: Bonnet: absorbent pad on a rotary machine, surface clean, quick drying
Dry compound: powder brushed in and vacuumed out, almost no water
Hot water extraction: spray and suck back, deepest clean, longer drying
Chooses bonnet or dry compound for quick turnaround or busy areas
Chooses extraction for scheduled deep cleans in empty rooms

practical1.title: Vacuum a guest room carpet and remove stains
practical1.brief: As a group, prepare the carpet in the bedroom of the Centre's mock villa (or a carpeted training room) for a guest's arrival. The assessor will put some made-up stains on spare carpet pieces or a rug, such as coffee, ketchup or curry sauce, chewing gum and lipstick, and will hide a few small items such as coins and an earring in the room. Work in these stages: (1) check the vacuum cleaner and plan who does what; (2) pick up small items, hand any guest items to the assessor, and move light furniture; (3) vacuum the carpet with slow, overlapping strokes from the far corner to the door, using the crevice tool for edges and the upholstery tool on the chair; (4) find out what each stain is and choose a product; (5) test the product on a hidden spot; (6) remove each stain by blotting and working from the outside in, then rinse and blot dry; (7) groom the pile, put back the furniture and check the room; (8) fill in a stain record saying what each stain was, what you used and the result. Every member vacuums part of the room and removes at least one stain while the assessor watches. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Vacuum cleaner with crevice and upholstery tools
Carpet spotting products for water-based and grease stains, with labels and SDS
Clean white cloths, a blunt knife or spoon, and a spray bottle of clean water
Ice in a bag (or a freeze spray made for carpets)
Spare carpet pieces or a rug with made-up stains
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The vacuum being checked, and the small items found
Vacuuming in overlapping strokes, cable behind
The crevice tool used along the skirting
Each stain before treatment, with its name
The product tested on a hidden spot
The finished room and the completed stain record
checklist: Checked the plug, cable and bag before vacuuming
Picked up small items and handed in guest items
Vacuumed with slow, overlapping strokes and used tools for edges and the chair
Named the stain type and chose a suitable product
Tested the product on a hidden spot first
Blotted, did not rub, and worked from the outside in
Rinsed and blotted dry without over-wetting, and groomed the pile
Filled in the stain record correctly
Switched off and unplugged, stored the equipment and took a full part in the group
safety: Check every plug and cable; do not use damaged equipment
Keep the cable behind you and out of walkways
Read labels and the SDS, wear gloves, keep the room aired and never mix products; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
Use a blunt knife or spoon only, cutting away from your body
Switch off and unplug before changing tools or emptying the vacuum

practical2.title: Deep clean a rug and an upholstered chair
practical2.brief: As a group, deep clean a rug and an upholstered chair from the Centre's mock villa using a hot water extraction machine with an upholstery tool. Work in these stages: (1) read the rug's label and the chair's cleaning code, and decide together whether each can be wet cleaned (if the chair's code does not allow water, vacuum and brush it only and say why); (2) check the machine, plug and cable; (3) vacuum the rug and chair thoroughly; (4) pre-treat stains and dirty areas as the label says; (5) mix the solution as the label says and fill the clean tank; (6) clean the rug in overlapping strokes with extra dry passes, and clean the chair with the upholstery tool without soaking it; (7) groom the pile and set up fans or airflow to dry them, with the rug raised or flat in the shade; (8) empty and rinse both tanks, clean the machine, and write a short report of what was done and any damage found. Every member uses the machine on part of the rug or chair while the assessor watches. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Hot water extraction machine with floor and upholstery tools, and the maker's instructions
Carpet and upholstery cleaning solution and pre-spray, with labels and SDS
A rug and an upholstered chair
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The rug label and the chair's cleaning code
The machine checked and the solution measured
Cleaning the rug in overlapping strokes
Cleaning the chair with the upholstery tool
The groomed rug and chair drying with fans

checklist: Read the label and cleaning code and made a correct decision on the method
Checked the machine, plug and cable before use
Mixed the solution as the label says and wore gloves and eye protection
Used overlapping strokes and dry passes without over-wetting
Cleaned the chair without soaking it
Groomed the pile and set up good airflow for drying
Emptied, rinsed and cleaned the machine
Wrote a clear report and took a full part in the group
safety: Use the machine only as trained, and follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
Keep plugs and cables away from water, and switch off and unplug before emptying tanks
Wear gloves and eye protection with cleaning solutions; never mix products
Put out wet floor signs; the floor round the rug may be slippery
Get help to lift or move a wet rug, and lift with bent knees
